title: Cross-SDK dependency sweep and deprecation cleanup for client surface
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Perform a coordinated dependency sweep across Python, Node, and Go client libraries to remove deprecated API surface, pin transitive dependencies to tested versions, and eliminate legacy compatibility shims that add maintenance burden and obscure performance regressions. The goal is to reduce the client maintenance window, remove risky unpinned transitive packages, and simplify the public surface so users get clearer upgrade paths with fewer runtime surprises.
background: Over the past 18 months we accumulated several compatibility shims (legacy request fields, alternate transport adapters, and ad-hoc polyfills) to support older consumers during runtime upgrades. These shims complicate test matrices, increase bundle sizes, and occasionally mask issues that only surface in production. Recent SDK test flakiness correlates with two unpinned deps in the JS client and one obsolete retry helper in Python. Go client has diverged on the error type hierarchy which increases churn in backend integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned versions for critical transitive deps in Python/JS/Go and updated lockfiles committed
Deprecated request fields removed from public docs and SDKs with backwards-compatibility migration guide
Compatibility shims gated behind an opt-in compatibility flag for one release, then removed
All client libraries pass the full CI compatibility matrix (linux/mac/windows where applicable) and the integration smoke test against runtime-1.18
Security review completed for any dependency upgrades that touch crypto or transport stacks
Performance regression benchmark shows no >5% latency regression on standard generate path
tasks: Audit client dependency trees and generate compatibility matrix (owner: Miguel)
Open PRs for lockfile regeneration and transitive pinning in each repo (py/js/go)
Implement a temporary --compat-mode flag in SDKs that preserves legacy fields for one release
Add e2e tests covering removed fields and migration paths
Coordinate deprecation notice and migration guide in docs.redwood.com (PM + Docs)
Submit security review for grpc/tls/crypto dependency changes
Run perf harness and update Optimize recommendations if behavior changes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Upgrading transitive deps could break downstream users. Mitigation: stagger rollout, opt-in compat flag, and provide clear migration guide and examples.
Risk: Removing shims may reveal latent server-side assumptions. Mitigation: add integration smoke tests against staging and runtime-1.18 canary with traffic shadowing.
Risk: CI flakiness due to new pinned versions. Mitigation: run expanded CI matrix and add flaky test quarantines before cutover.
notes: Prefer non-breaking minor upgrades where possible; document any semver-major in CHANGELOG with migration steps.
For JS: target Node 18+ LTS and align package-lock/yarn lock regeneration strategy across mono-repo boundaries.
For Python: prefer constraints.txt-style pins in CI to avoid local dev drift; communicate new constraints to developers.
For Go: update go.mod replacements and add migration notes for error type changes that affect callers.
